38304-encyclopaedia-britannica-11th-edit:
This file holds a slice of the eleventh edition of the Encyclopaedia Britannica, the Cambridge edition of 1910 and 1911. Its range runs from the theory of groups to the entries under Gw. The transcriber's notes record small corrections in four articles. They concern the Guadalquivir river, Guanajuato, guarantee, and the guinea fowl.

The Guadalquivir article traces the Spanish river's two channels rejoining near Cadiz. Guanajuato is placed in a rich mining district of Mexico, with prosperous Acambaro to its south. The guarantee article cites the Egyptian codes on contracts made for persons without legal capacity. Such slices preserve the edition's method: mathematics, geography, law, and natural history side by side, each by a specialist, in alphabetical democracy.
podcast-dannyjones-pt5CbCTmAgw:
Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb joins Danny Jones to say he thinks aliens may be trying to reach us. Loeb is a top space scientist known for his hunt for alien tech near Earth. He argues the search should be bold and open.

Loeb talks about odd space rocks, signals, and the case for craft from other stars. He faults his peers for fear of the topic. Jones asks what find would prove him right once and for all. Listeners get the case from the best known name in the field. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
